Below the text, at the right, the word "IDEM" on its own line. Page number at the head. No margin notes. Faint marks at the right edge of the text block are show-through or the edge of the neighbouring page, not text.

main_text.p: rum eruditissimus Allatius mihi videtur huic operi coronidem impofuisse, atque omne, vt aiunt, tulisse punctum. Quod ipsum tibi optimo rerum æstimatori, & aliis viris doctissimis audio summopere probari. D.O.M. Reuerendissimam Dominationem tuam ad Eccle-sia Patauina bonum, & nobilissimam familiam tuam ornamentum diutissime tueatur incolumem. Patauij ex meis ædibus VIII. Idus Nouem-bris, anno Christi MDCXXX.
main_text.head: LAVRENTIVS PIGNORIVS Eidem.
main_text.p: Percurri, vt tu imperasti, Commentarium Leonis Allatij, conscriptum aduersus impostu-ram male feriatorum quorundam, qui Ioan-nam, nescio quam, Papissam nobis obtrudere sunt conati. Is mihi adeo sapidus est visus, vt bis, terque regustare libuerit. Multos equidem vidi, qui idem argumentum tractauerunt, non sine laude: at vero qui adeo perite collimauerit, adhuc neminem. Ego sane gratulor Auctori, quem rogatum velim, vt ad huiusmodi conscriptiones conferat stylum, quo multis misere deceptis lux aliqua tandem veritatis affulgeat. Vale. Vir Reuerendissime, non sine insigni a me gratiarum actione. Domi.

page.notes: The text is clear throughout. The printed long s is rendered as plain s, and the double-s ligature (ss) is transcribed as ss (impofuisse, tulisse, Papissam). The Greek letters on this page are absent. The printed "Domi." is probably a truncated place name or abbreviation; kept as printed. The "non_" at the line end is a printed line-end mark, transcribed as "non". The space in "VirReuerendiffime" appears to be a printing gap; written as "Vir Reuerendissime".
